efet_body:
Rajasthan Health Minister directs medical colleges to enforce zero-tolerance policy against ragging
He also warned that college authorities would also face disciplinary action if found negligent

Rajasthan Health Minister Gajendra Singh Khimsar. File. (Photo: Facebook/gajendrakhimsar)
Rajasthan
Health Minister Gajendra Singh Khimsar on Monday (November 16, 2026) directed all government and private medical colleges to enforce a zero-tolerance policy against ragging.
He also warned that college authorities would also face disciplinary action if found negligent.
He said action would be taken against officials found guilty of laxity as well as students involved in ragging cases.
Also read |
Central University of Rajasthan establishes first learner support centre in Jaipur
"The minister has directed officials of the Medical Education Department and Rajasthan Medical Education Society (RAJMES) to ensure compliance with the anti-ragging action plan in all government and private medical colleges in the state to check cases of ragging,” according to a release.
The minister said senior students forcing juniors to stay awake late at night, participate in activities against their wishes, face humiliation or undergo any form of harassment constitutes serious indiscipline.
He said college administrations must ensure a safe environment for students and investigate every complaint promptly and impartially.
He instructed officials to take prompt action in ragging cases. The minister said that the identity of the victim student should not be revealed and action against those who exert pressure to withdraw the complaints should be taken.
"There should be fair investigation in all cases of ragging," he said.

View Market Dashboard Old Monk sales ban: Rum maker withdraws court plea, agrees to revise labels after FSSAI objections Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries, which makes Old Monk, has withdrawn its Bombay High Court petition challenging an FSSAI order restricting the sale and distribution of certain products. The company told the court it would revise the labels and submit them to the regulator for approval. Anjali Thakur Published 7 Nov 2026, 06:49 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Old Monk sales ban: Rum maker withdraws court plea, agrees to revise labels after FSSAI objections ( Instagram/oldmonk_indiaa ) AI Quick Read Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries Pvt Ltd, the maker of the Old Monk rum brand, has withdrawn its petition before the Bombay High Court challenging a sales restriction imposed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over the labelling and product descriptions of certain variants. FSSAI had objected to the use of the term "rum" on products containing added flavouring agents, directing that they be labelled and marketed as "rum-flavoured spirit" instead. The regulator had also raised concerns over descriptions such as "7 Years Old Blended" and "Very Old Vatted". The authority had barred the sale and distribution of several Old Monk products manufactured at the company's Khopoli facility. Also Read | Tanvi Patri’s father recalls Youth Olympics final heartbreak: ‘Papa, I lost…’ Old Monk maker agrees to revise product labels During a hearing on Thursday, a bench led by Chief Justice Maheshchandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna was informed by the company that it would revise the product labels and submit the updated versions to FSSAI for approval. The company's decision to withdraw its petition follows the court's refusal to grant interim relief against the regulator's order. Why did FSSAI restrict the sale of certain Old Monk products? The dispute centres on the classification and labelling of certain Old Monk variants. FSSAI's objection was that products containing added flavouring agents should be described as "rum-flavoured spirit" rather than "rum". The regulator also questioned the use of age-related and product descriptions such as "7 Years Old Blended" and "Very Old Vatted". Also Read | Diwali Muhurat trading: Why do NSE, BSE open for live trading session on Diwali? The sales and distribution restriction applied to several products manufactured at the company's Khopoli facility. Old Monk maker had cited over ₹ 350 crore loss in excise revenue The brewer had earlier argued that the sales restriction had resulted in a loss of more than ₹ 350 crore in excise revenue for the Maharashtra government. Also Read | Liam Lawson faces uncertain F1 future as Racing Bulls delay 2027 decision However, after the Bombay High Court declined to grant interim relief against the FSSAI order, the company chose not to pursue the case on merits and withdrew its petition. The court subsequently disposed of the matter. FSSAI cracks down on unsafe food, suspends licence, orders recall
In a major regulatory crackdown to safeguard consumer health, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has taken stern action against multiple food manufacturers, suspending the operational licence of a confectionery firm over grave hygiene lapses and ordering an immediate market recall of packaged cumin powder found to be "unsafe."

The regulator also flagged a dairy whitener sample as substandard, intensifying enforcement to protect consumer health.
In a major regulatory crackdown to safeguard consumer health, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has taken stern action against multiple food manufacturers, suspending the operational licence of a confectionery firm over grave
hygiene lapses
and ordering an immediate market recall of packaged cumin powder found to be "unsafe."
According to regulatory directives, the manufacturing licence of a bakery and confectionery manufacturing unit has been suspended with immediate effect after food safety authorities discovered critical non-compliance and severe deficiencies in sanitation and hygienic practices during inspections.
Under the enforcement order, the manufacturing unit has been barred from producing or distributing its products until standard sanitary protocols are strictly met and verified by the regulator.
In a separate enforcement measure, the food safety authority has directed a prominent spice manufacturing firm to execute an immediate nationwide recall of its "Pre-packed Cumin Powder".
The recall directive was issued after official laboratory analysis declared samples of the packaged product "UNSAFE" for human consumption under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
The FBO was further directed to undertake corrective measures to prevent recurrence of the incident and submit a report upon completion of the recall.
Earlier on Saturday, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said a sample of low-fat dairy whitener manufactured by a food brand and collected from the premises of a hotel chain in Connaught Place, New Delhi, has been declared "substandard" and "unsafe" in a Food Analyst's laboratory report under the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006.
According to the findings, the sample was drawn from the premises of the hotel chain in Connaught Place in the national capital. The Food Analyst's laboratory report found the sample to be "substandard" and "unsafe", indicating non-compliance with the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006.
A copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the Food Business Operator (FBO) for reference and necessary action.
Following the findings, a notice was issued to the hotel chain regarding the non-compliant product.
